description: Writing a LINQ query as chained extension method calls such as `Where`, `Select` and `GroupBy`, each taking a lambda.
The SQL-like `from ... where ... select` form that the compiler translates into the same method calls, with no semantic or performance difference.
Shaping each element into a new type with `Select`, usually an anonymous type inside a method or a record when the result leaves it.
One group produced by `GroupBy`, exposing its `Key` and enumerable as the elements that share that key.
An operator such as `First`, `FirstOrDefault`, `Single` or `SingleOrDefault` that returns one element and differs in how it treats zero or several matches.
A one-to-many dictionary built by `ToLookup`, which returns an empty sequence for a missing key instead of throwing.
A .NET 10 LINQ operator that keeps every element of the first sequence and passes `null` to the result selector when the second has no match.
An operator that turns an empty sequence into one holding a single `default` element, so a following `Max` returns `0` instead of throwing.
